`StepConfig::prompt_source()` is DEAD — zero callers in production, tests, or the sdk; `cargo check --lib -p ziee` emits `warning: method \`prompt_source\` is never used` on this exact line. It was added (ITEM-9/api-friendliness) precisely to stop callers passing the two adjacent same-typed opposite-meaning `&Option<String>` args to the free `prompt_source(a, b)` — and its own doc says 'Preferred over calling prompt_source(a, b) directly' — yet validate.rs:714 and dispatch.rs:130, the only two consumers in the tree, both call the free function directly. The ergonomic hazard it names is still 100% present at every site, including `load_raw_prompt`/`resolve_prompt`, whose narrowed signatures put `prompt` and `prompt_file` adjacent. Either wire it at both call sites or delete it (CODING_GUIDELINES §15: dead code = unfinished work).

The doc block at 266-280 is two merged doc comments attached to the WRONG item. Lines 266-275 ('The `(prompt, prompt_file)` pair for the kinds that HAVE one… Exhaustive on purpose… Adding a kind here is a compile error exactly once.') describe `prompt_fields()`, but they sit on `prompt_source()` — and are then followed, mid-block, by a second opening summary line ('[`prompt_source`] for this step, or `None` for a kind with no prompt.'), which is a rustdoc summary in the middle of a paragraph. `prompt_fields()` at line 285 — the accessor that actually carries the exhaustive match and the compile-error guarantee, and the one every real caller uses — has NO doc comment at all. So the ITEM-9 rationale is documented on a dead function and absent from the live one.

`PromptFileError::code()` and `::layer()` are `pub` with ZERO callers anywhere (grep across src/ and tests/ finds only the doc comment at 1337 that NAMES them). They restate, in two exhaustive matches, exactly the variant→code and variant→layer mapping that `prompt_file_finding()` (1343) implements a second time with literal arguments. That is the same rule in two places in the same language — the duplication this change's own premise says it removed — with nothing binding the copies: `prompt_file_finding` could map Empty to WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE and `code()` would still say FILE_MISSING, silently. Worse for extensibility: adding a `PromptFileError` variant produces compile errors in `code()`/`layer()` FIRST, so a maintainer satisfies the dead pair and reasonably believes the mapping is done. Delete the pair, or make `prompt_file_finding` the only mapping and give the drift guard a way to read it.

Dependency direction. The RUNNER now performs its production prompt read by calling into the VALIDATOR: `crate::modules::workflow::validate::read_prompt_file`. `read_prompt_file` is not validation logic — it is filesystem I/O (openat2/O_NOFOLLOW via libc, fstat type check, byte cap, bounded read, UTF-8 decode) that happens to also be the check. The workflow module already owns a neutral home for exactly this (`file_io.rs`, which already holds `write_step_output` and its own size cap). Putting it in `validate.rs` pushes that file to 3,974 lines, makes `validate` a libc-touching I/O module, and means any future consumer of 'read a bundle-relative file safely' has to depend on the validator. Move `read_prompt_file` + `check_prompt_file_shape` + `PromptFileError` + `MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES` + `open_confined` to `file_io.rs` and let both validate and dispatch depend on it — the shared-rule property is preserved and the direction stops being inverted.

Blocking I/O on the async executor, and inconsistently so within this one change. `dispatch.rs:133-139` deliberately wraps `read_prompt_file` in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` with an explicit comment ('it stats + reads, so it goes on the blocking pool rather than a tokio worker'). The validator path does not: `validate_for_install` -> `validate_collecting` -> `check_prompt_files` -> `read_prompt_file` is called synchronously from `async fn spawn_run` (runner.rs:1248), `async fn resume_run` (runner.rs:1552), and the install/import handlers (handlers/dev.rs:268, :564). Before this change `check_prompt_files` only did `canonicalize()`; it now opens and reads up to 1 MiB per prompt_file step on a tokio worker thread, on every launch and every resume. Either both go through spawn_blocking or neither does — the asymmetry means the reasoning written into dispatch.rs is contradicted three call sites away (CODING_GUIDELINES §5, 'No std::fs in async').

Scope: two NEW rejection reasons that DESIGN neither lists in §1's case table nor carves out in §3 ('this branch changes only what its own fix made wrong or left unguarded'). (1) `MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES = 1 MiB` — a bundle whose prompt_file exceeds it previously installed and ran and now fails install, spawn_run AND resume_run. (2) `check_prompt_file_shape` widens the pre-existing `contains("..") || starts_with('/')` reject to ALSO refuse any backslash and any `X:` drive prefix; a backslash is a legal filename character on Unix, so an existing bundle with `prompt_file: 'prompts/a\\b.md'` is now WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE. Both are defensible consequences of making the validator READ the file (which the design's direction does require), but each re-verdicts pre-existing bundles and neither appears in the document being conformed to. Record them in DESIGN (or in a §3 amendment) rather than only in PLAN ITEM-16.

Comment overstates. 'Those are the same two functions the validator's verdict is computed from, so a definition the validator reports green cannot fail here, and one it reports red cannot quietly succeed here (INV-1, both directions).' Stated unconditionally, this is false for the DRAFT validation surfaces: `POST /validate` and `POST /validate-def` pass a bundle root that deliberately does not exist, so `check_prompt_files` skips everything except the shape check (validate.rs:1396, 1413) — a def those endpoints report green CAN fail here on a bad prompt_file. DESIGN §3 carves that out explicitly; the comment does not, so a reader takes the guarantee to be universal. Add 'against a materialized bundle' to the sentence.

The TEST-1 agreement assertion is structurally unable to catch a rule removed from the SHARED function — which is most of what this change added. Proved by mutation: deleting the emptiness rejection from `read_prompt_file` removes it from the validator AND the runner symmetrically, so `prompt_findings.is_empty() == run.is_ok()` stays true on every one of the 120 rows. The mutation was caught, but by the `ran_ok == 18` anti-vacuity COUNT (which failed with 24) plus TEST-6 and TEST-3 — never by the implication itself. Worth stating in the test's own doc, because the count is the load-bearing assertion for the whole shared-file half and reads today like a secondary sanity check.

Visibility is wider than any consumer. `prompt_file_ref`, `check_prompt_file_shape`, `PromptFileError::{code,layer}`, and `MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES` are all `pub` but used only inside `validate.rs` (only `prompt_source`, `PromptSource`, `read_prompt_file`, `PROMPT_*_MESSAGE` and `VALIDATION_CODES` have an out-of-module consumer, all in dispatch.rs). Publishing the internal halves of a rule whose whole point is that there is ONE entry point invites a future caller to shape-check without reading, or to read without shape-checking — the exact split this change closed. `pub(crate)`/private for the four.
